questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Explore new cultures

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: I wanted to go to a destination where I knew the culture already and had a deep fondness for it prior to my exchange, and immerse myself in the culture and language, while also having the opportunity to travel around which Milan is a great home base for.

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: I learned many things about myself and how to take care of myself in a foreign country. There were a couple of downsides to it such as occasional loneliness and homesickness, but overall I would not trade my experience for anything.

questions.question: How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: The University of Copenhagen was very helpful with any inquiries I had, otherwise, I could find all information I needed. The University of Milan was more confusing, but it was no problem reaching out to those in charge and figuring out what I needed to know.

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: The Erasmus Student Network (ESN) in Milan was helpful and sent out information regarding various things upon arrival and how to get involved in social activities. The university also provided information on how to choose classes and afterward how to sign up for exams, etc.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
questions.answer: It was confusing at first, but everything worked out and we all managed to figure it out.

questions.question: How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing on my own

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: Off campus

questions.question: How easy was it to find off campus housing? Any recommendations? *
questions.answer: It was not the easiest thing since it is very expensive to live in Milan and we were four people who had to find an apartment at a reasonable price. We looked on airbnb and spotahome, and found an alright apartment for an alright price.

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living off campus? *
questions.answer: It is rather expensive, but it is possible to find something, and there can be issues with the landlord, who might not be very good at English. Also, it is not necessary to live right in the center of the city as public transportation is good, but keep in mind the metro closes around 1 am each night.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: I did not choose to live in student housing.

questions.question: How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: It was not as simple as I find it here in KU, since the UNIMI website is confusing when it comes to courses and finding the syllabus. Additionally, we had to compare previous semesters' courses and classes to check for any overlapping classes.

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: Reaching out to the university.

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: I registered for all the classes I wanted that were available for the semester.

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Relax, and keep an open mind, as well as reserve half a day or so to finish registrations.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: The courses offered in English were not very academically challenging, and some were not completely what I expected. Exams were more creative in some courses, but many courses had oral exams.

questions.question: Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: MA

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: The academic level was not very high in most of my courses however some courses had very engaging and passionate professors who had a high academic level.

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: It was mostly listening to the professor speak, who would only ask questions occasionally during one class. There was much less need for preparation before each class, and there was very limited group work among students.

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer:
Gender Justice
Negotiation, Mediation, and Sustainable Conflict Resolution
Law, Culture, and Development in a Global World
Smart Cities, Artificial Intelligence, and Digital Transformation Law 
International Commercial and Investment Arbitration

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: I would recommend Gender Justice for the exams and curriculum as well as the professor who was very passionate about her topic and teaching. I would also recommend Negotiation as it was not a very legal course and also had a big element of psychology. Keep in mind that a part of the grade consists of doing a recorded negotiation simulation in groups. And Smart Cities had a very easy written exam. I would NOT recommend the arbitration course because of the professor who is very unserious and not mindful of the students, and is very harsh at the oral exam.

What unexpected costs did you encounter? *
questions.answer: Electric bill.

questions.question: What items were more or less expensive than you expected? *
questions.answer: Less expensive to travel around than I had expected and possible to find cheap rooms if necessary.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: The ESN offered many activities for students, both local and international students.

questions.question: What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Those that the ESN offered.

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: Traveling around since Milan is perfectly located for travels around the north of Italy and as well as neighboring countries.

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer: Weekend trips around the country, going out to restaurants, seeing the city (museums, cultural sites, the opera, going to the top of the Duomo)

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: For me very easy, but it requires an interest in immersing yourself in the culture and wanting to experience the local life and stay positive and keep and open mind about the people and the culture.

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: Find a common interest or sit with other people in the class and not just other Danish or international students and just go for it. Italians are very open and welcoming.

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: There were no cultural differences I found challenging.

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: The language and the mentality of the people.

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer: Keep an open mind, and chose courses both based on your interest and also the difficulty. I would also recommend living with at least one other person since you might encounter problems with your landlord and it is better to not be alone in the situation, and you will have a home base and not get too lonely during the exams period.

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: Nothing I can think of.

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: Learning the language and living with the Italian mentality and culture.

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: Living in the moment.

questions.question: Any other comments?
questions.answer: No comments.

questions.question: Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
